The argument validation process fails when passing a vault-encrypted value to a no_log role parameter

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

validate_argument_spec

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version

  config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
```

```console
# if using a version older than ansible-core 2.12 you should omit the '-t all'
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all
CONFIG_FILE() = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
```


### OS / Environment

Arch Linux (Rolling Release)

### Steps to Reproduce

```yaml
# roles/validated_args/meta/argument_specs.yml
argument_specs:
  main:
    options:
      my_token:
        no_log: True
```

```yaml
# roles/validated_args/tasks/main.yml
- debug:
    var: my_token
```

```yaml
# validate_args.yml
- hosts: localhost
  vars:
    my_token: !vault |
          $ANSIBLE_VAULT;1.1;AES256
          32336162303235386136653837646531653032623266366434313839646630653434623161393433
          3533363934643334313436663363616133663232613731330a323062376464653663666136646364
          66653765646336393765366264343337386631373238613235356264643835653132336164373433

          62616364666366613033623062396438356338316665356462356631363263366265
  roles:
    - validated_args
```

To reproduce:

```sh
echo '1234' > pwdfile # Write dummy vault password file
ansible-playbook --vault-password-file=pwdfile validate_args.yml
```

I expected the playbook to run, and treat the decrypted value of the `my_token` parameter as a value to mask from the log output

items.body:
##### SUMMARY
I use blockinfile and block is taken from variable like this:
```yaml
    foo_block: |
      {
      {% for i in a_list_of_strings %}
        '{{ i }}',
      {% endfor %}
      }
```
It fails with some weird internal errors. 

If I remove single quotes around `{{ i }}` it's not failing.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
blockinfile

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
```
ansible 2.7.1
  config file = /home/etam/.ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/etam/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3.6/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.6.5 (default, Mar 31 2018, 19:45:04) [GCC]
```

##### CONFIGURATION
```
ANSIBLE_NOCOWS(/home/etam/.ansible.cfg) = True
```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
OS: openSUSE Tumbleweed, snapshot 20181116

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
`inventory.yml`:
```yaml
all:
  hosts:
    localhost:
      ansible_connection: local
  vars:
    ansible_python_interpreter: /usr/bin/python3
```

`play.yml`:
```yaml
- hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: no
  vars:
    a_list_of_strings:
      - "a"
      - "b"
      - "c"
      - "d"
    foo_block: |
      {
      {% for i in a_list_of_strings %}
        '{{ i }}',
      {% endfor %}
      }
  tasks:
    - blockinfile:
        path: /tmp/foo.txt
        create: yes
        state: present
        block: "{{ bar_block }}"
```

##### EXPECTED RESULTS
`/tmp/foo.txt` should contain
```

{
  'a',
  'b',
  'c',
  'd',
}
```

items.title: sub plugins are not being pulled into documentation or ansible-doc etc

labels.name: docs
labels.description: This issue/PR relates to or includes documentation.

items.body:
### Summary

Some collections, such as ansible.utils, have an entity called sub_plugins that include DOCUMENTATION blocks that are not visible in docs.ansible.com or probably not in `ansible-doc`.  These sub_plugins are important to end users and their information should be displayed.

Examples of sub_plugins:

https://github.com/ansible-collections/ansible.utils/tree/main/plugins/sub_plugins

### Issue Type

Documentation Report

### Component Name

docs/docsite/rst/

### Ansible Version

```console
2.9, 2.11
```


### Configuration

```console
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed
```


### OS / Environment

Fedora 33

### Additional Information

This added information will improve the user experience.

labels.name: module
labels.description: This issue/PR relates to a module.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: This issue/PR relates to a bug.

labels.name: has_pr
labels.description: This issue has an associated PR.

labels.name: feature
labels.description: This issue/PR relates to a feature request.

items.body:
##### ISSUE TYPE

~Feature  Idea~
Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME

pause module

##### ANSIBLE VERSION

2.3

##### SUMMARY

From @bobrik on 2015-06-01T10:43:32Z
It would be nice to about sequence if operator does not respond in timeout. Currently `pause` module can only continue if no action taken. Extra flag like `action_on_timeout` with values `abort` and `continue` would do the trick.

Copied from original issue: ansible/ansible-modules-core#1449
